entities.summary: William Maitland of Lethington was a Scottish politician and reformer who played a significant role in the early modern period. He was the eldest son of poet Richard Maitland and served as a diplomat and advisor to various Scottish and English monarchs. Maitland's efforts to modernize Scotland's legal system and promote Protestantism contributed to the country's Protestant Reformation. He also played a key role in the Thirty Years' War, serving as a delegate to the Peace of Westphalia. Maitland's legacy can be seen in the modern Scottish legal system and the Protestant faith of the Scottish people. The Scottish Reformation, which Maitland helped to shape, had far-reaching consequences for the country's politics, society, and culture. As a diplomat, Maitland helped to negotiate the Treaty of Edinburgh, which established a permanent alliance between Scotland and England. In 1573, Maitland was appointed as the Lord Advocate of Scotland, a position he held until his death. He died on June 9, 1573, at the age of approximately 52. Maitland's impact on Scottish history cannot be overstated, and his contributions to the country's politics, religion, and culture continue to be felt today.
